input: Hi, I wanted to check in on invoice #1048 — it has been overdue for two weeks. Could you let me know when the payment will be sent?
polite_rewrite: Hello, I hope you are doing well. I wanted to follow up on invoice #1048, which is now two weeks overdue. Could you please share when the payment will be sent? Thank you so much!
explanation: A gentle follow-up with a clear date request keeps the tone professional instead of pushy.

input: I underestimated the work on the product photos and the deadline is in two days. I need to ask for three more days.
polite_rewrite: Hi, I owe you an honest update on the product photos: the remaining work is bigger than I first thought. A few more days would let me finish it properly, and I will keep you updated daily until it is done. Thank you!
explanation: Owning the misjudgement and offering daily updates rebuilds trust.

input: The client asked for a fifth revision of the logo and my contract allows two. I need to charge for the extra rounds.
polite_rewrite: Hello, I am glad to keep refining the logo. We have now used the two revision rounds in our agreement, so further rounds will be billed at my hourly rate. Shall I go ahead with this round and add it to the invoice?
explanation: Counting the rounds factually makes the extra charge expected, not surprising.
